# Reflex 1.3.9
## Hide system menu-bar icons
- The Hidden/Visible panel now includes native system icons on macOS 27: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, battery, sound, displays, input sources, the clock, and Control Center. - Hide icons individually without disabling their underlying services. Your choices persist across restart, and clicking Reflex reveals them again. - Siri, Time Machine, and other legacy system extras appear as a labelled group because macOS hides them together. Apple apps with their own menu-bar icons are also supported. - Reflex's own icon stays available. System controls that cannot be managed independently are labelled rather than given nonfunctional hide buttons. - The accepted macOS 27 limitation remains: Now Playing, user switching, and camera/microphone controls disappear while collapsed and return on reveal. - Older macOS versions keep the existing divider-based behavior. Existing app-hiding choices and other Reflex workflows are unchanged.

# Reflex 1.3.8
## Menu-bar compatibility with macOS 27
- Restores the Hidden and Visible lists on macOS 27 using Accessibility-based app discovery. - Adds saved per-app hiding on macOS 27. Apps start visible; use the minus button to choose which to hide. Multiple icons from one app are managed together. - On macOS 27, collapsing also temporarily hides Apple's Now Playing, user-switching, and camera/microphone controls. Click Reflex to reveal them, or turn off Hide Menu Bar Items to keep them visible. Their underlying services are unaffected. - Revealing items, disabling hiding, or quitting Reflex restores the icons. Failed or timed-out hiding attempts release the restriction. - The macOS 27 panel uses application icons; use the native menu bar to rearrange items instead of dragging within the panel. - Preserves the existing divider, icon capture, and rearranging behavior on macOS 15 through 26. - Other Reflex workflows, including clipboard history and Codex Micro shortcuts, are unchanged.

# Reflex 1.3.7
## Clipboard history without accidental drawers
- Removed the shake gesture, drag-and-drop drawer, and floating clipboard shelf. - Clipboard history remains available from the right-click menu, with search, screenshot OCR, and click-to-copy. - Keeps clipboard URL rewrites, copy/paste bypass shortcuts, Codex Micro mappings, and Option-drag window tiling unchanged.

# Reflex 1.3.6
## Tab from the Codex Micro knob
- Pressing the upper-left Codex Micro knob now sends a native Tab key press in any application. - Keeps knob rotation and joystick navigation behavior unchanged. - Releases Tab safely if Reflex is paused, the mapping is disabled, or the Micro disconnects mid-press.

# Reflex 1.3.5
## Keep Apple Music out of the way
- Prevents Apple Music from opening when macOS uses it as the idle Play-key fallback. - Leaves native Play/Pause routing untouched for active audio and video apps. - Adds a saved right-click menu toggle for temporarily allowing Music launches.

# Reflex 1.3.4
## More intentional clipboard gestures
- Adds Option-Command-V to paste the exact original text once after Reflex rewrites a copied URL. - Restores the transformed clipboard after the raw paste without overwriting newer clipboard contents. - Makes the clipboard drawer require a wider, faster mouse shake to prevent accidental triggers while dragging.

# Reflex 1.3.3
## Faster Codex Micro navigation
- Moves the Codex Micro dial through adjacent Codex sidebar chats instead of navigation history. - Repeats joystick scrolling while held in Codex, Chrome, and Slack. - Accelerates scrolling smoothly as the joystick is pushed farther.

# Reflex 1.3.2
## Four-way Codex Micro navigation
- Maps joystick right and left to forward and back in Codex, Chrome, and Slack. - Maps joystick up and down to ordinary pointer-targeted scrolling in all three apps. - Fires once per directional entry while preserving the existing focused Codex dial scrolling.

# Reflex 1.3.1
## Codex Micro startup repair
- Fixes the deterministic launch crash when a Codex Micro is already connected. - Registers the passive raw-report callback once at the HID manager level before activation, as required by IOKit. - Keeps reconnect, pause, shutdown, mappings, lighting, and device firmware behavior unchanged.

# Reflex 1.3.0
## Codex Micro controls
- F13 now foregrounds Codex or starts a new task when Codex is already active; F15 foregrounds Slack; F14 foregrounds the default browser. - The dial moves through adjacent Slack conversations and Chrome tabs, and scrolls the focused Codex conversation when Codex is foregrounded. - The upper directional control moves backward and forward through Slack or Chrome history. - Repeated same-direction dial turns now arrive through the raw passive HID report stream without dropped detents or duplicate handling. - A local, nonactivating Input Diagnostics panel makes device behavior inspectable without collecting anything while it is closed.
